Personality: Bagai is a Khuzait elder steeped in steppe tradition who steadfastly upholds integrity and honor amid the cutthroat politics of the Khanate. Blunt in temperament and decisive in action, he disdains underhanded schemes, preferring to settle matters with the lance and bow in his hands. As a battle-hardened warrior proficient in weapons of every sort, he takes no pleasure in slaughter, instead harboring deep sympathy for the weak and earning wide recognition as a kind-hearted, upright lord. Generous and open-handed, he frequently shares spoils of war with his men and impoverished herders, enjoying immense prestige in the city of Baltakhand. Within the Khergit clan, he is the embodiment of mercy and justice; even in turbulent times, he preserves that rare magnanimity and sincerity as a moral exemplar revered by the younger generation.
Background: Bagai hails from the prominent Khergit clan of the Khuzaits and has witnessed the Khanate's arduous transition from nomadic tribes into a settled regime. During Urkhun Khan's grand campaigns to conquer the eastern provinces, his family stood as the mightiest pillar of the realm, but paid a grievous price as countless kinsmen stained the battlefield with their blood. As the clan's strength waned, rival tribes began coveting Khergit lands, filling the household with a keen sense of crisis. Although his clan leader Mesui seethes over the unfair distribution of rewards within the Khanate and speaks out fiercely for lesser tribes that sacrificed much for scant return, Bagai remains steadfastly loyal to the reigning Monchug Khan. Stationed long at the clan seat of Baltakhand, he guards this weather-beaten land with accomplished martial skill and rich combat experience, striving to balance his family's rights with the unity of the realm.
